sanskrit: tac chrutvā bhāṣitaṃ tasya śatrughnasya mahātmanaḥ krodham āhārayat tīvraṃ tiṣṭha tiṣṭheti cābravīt
english: Hearing those words of the great-souled Śatrughna, Lavaṇa roused fierce anger and cried out repeatedly, "Stand! Stand!"

sanskrit: pāṇau pāṇiṃ viniṣpiṣya dantān kaṭakaṭāyya ca lavaṇo raghuśārdūlam āhvayām āsa cāsakṛt
english: Slapping palm against palm and grinding his teeth, Lavaṇa challenged the tiger of the Raghu line again and again.

sanskrit: taṃ bruvāṇaṃ tathā vākyaṃ lavaṇaṃ ghoravikramam śatrughno deva śatrughna idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: To Lavaṇa of terrible valour who spoke thus, Śatrughna, destroyer of enemies, spoke these words.

sanskrit: śatrughno na tadā jāto yadānye nirjitās tvayā tad adya bāṇābhihato vraja taṃ yamasādanam
english: "Śatrughna was not yet born when others were conquered by you; but today, struck by my arrow, go to the abode of Yama."

sanskrit: ṛṣayo 'py adya pāpātman mayā tvāṃ nihataṃ raṇe paśyantu viprā vidvāṃsas tridaśā iva rāvaṇam
english: "Today, O evil-souled one, let the sages, the learned brāhmaṇas, and the gods witness you slain in battle by me, even as they witnessed Rāvaṇa."

sanskrit: tvayi madbāṇanirdagdhe patite 'dya niśācara puraṃ janapadaṃ cāpi kṣemam etad bhaviṣyati
english: "When you, O night-roamer, are scorched by my arrow and fallen today, this city and the countryside will be at peace."

sanskrit: adya madbāhuniṣkrāntaḥ śaro vajranibhānanaḥ pravekṣyate te hṛdayaṃ padmam aṃśur ivārkajaḥ
english: "Today the arrow released from my arm, its face like a thunderbolt, will enter your lotus-heart as a ray enters that of the sun's son."

sanskrit: evam ukto mahāvṛkṣaṃ lavaṇaḥ krodhamūrchitaḥ śatrughnorasi cikṣepa taṃ śūraḥ śatadhācchinat
english: Addressed thus, Lavaṇa, swooning with rage, hurled a great tree at the chest of Śatrughna; the hero cut it to a hundred pieces.

sanskrit: tad dṛṣṭvā viphalaṃ karma rākṣasaḥ punar eva tu pādapān subahūn gṛhya śatrughne vyasṛjad balī
english: Seeing that act rendered fruitless, the powerful rākṣasa seized a great many trees and hurled them again at Śatrughna.

sanskrit: śatrughnaś cāpi tejasvī vṛkṣān āpatato bahūn tribhiś caturbhir ekaikaṃ ciccheda nataparvabhiḥ
english: The brilliant Śatrughna severed those many oncoming trees one by one with three or four arrows whose joints were smooth.

sanskrit: tato bāṇamayaṃ varṣaṃ vyasṛjad rākṣasor asi śatrughno vīryasaṃpanno vivyathe na ca rākṣasaḥ
english: Then Śatrughna, endowed with valour, discharged a rain of arrows at the rākṣasa's body, yet the rākṣasa was not distressed.

sanskrit: tataḥ prahasya lavaṇo vṛkṣam utpāṭya līlayā śirasy abhyahanac chūraṃ srastāṅgaḥ sa mumoha vai
english: Then Lavaṇa laughed and, uprooting a tree with ease, struck the hero on the head; his limbs went limp and he fell into a swoon.

sanskrit: tasmin nipatite vīre hāhākāro mahān abhūt ṛṣīṇāṃ deva saṃghānāṃ gandharvāpsarasām api
english: When that hero fell, a great cry of "Ah! Ah!" arose from the hosts of sages, gods, Gandharvas, and Apsarases.

sanskrit: tam avajñāya tu hataṃ śatrughnaṃ bhuvi pātitam rakṣo labdhāntaram api na viveśa svam ālayam
english: Disdaining Śatrughna, though struck down and prostrate on the earth, the rākṣasa, even with the opportunity secured, did not enter his own dwelling.

sanskrit: nāpi śūlaṃ prajagrāha taṃ dṛṣṭvā bhuvi pātitam tato hata iti jñātvā tān bhakṣān samudāvahat
english: Nor did he take up his trident, seeing him fallen on the ground; thinking him slain, he then went off to gather his food.

sanskrit: muhūrtāl labdhasaṃjñas tu punas tasthau dhṛtāyudhaḥ śatrughno rākṣasadvāri ṛṣibhiḥ saṃprapūjitaḥ
english: But within a moment Śatrughna recovered consciousness and stood again, weapon in hand, at the rākṣasa's gate, honoured by the sages.

sanskrit: tato divyam amoghaṃ taṃ jagrāha śaram uttamam jvalantaṃ tejasā ghoraṃ pūrayantaṃ diśo daśa
english: Then he took up that supreme, infallible, divine arrow — blazing with energy, terrible, filling all ten directions.

sanskrit: vajrānanaṃ vajravegaṃ merumandara gauravam nataṃ parvasu sarveṣu saṃyugeṣv aparājitam
english: Its face was like a thunderbolt, its speed like a thunderbolt, its weight equal to Meru and Mandara; smooth at every joint, unconquered in all battles.

sanskrit: asṛkcandanadigdhāṅgaṃ cārupatraṃ patatriṇam dānavendrācalendrāṇām asurāṇāṃ ca dāruṇam
english: Its body smeared with blood-red sandalwood, with beautiful feathering; dreadful to lords of Dānavas, lords of mountains, and Asuras.

sanskrit: taṃ dīptam iva kālāgniṃ yugānte samupasthite dṛṣṭvā sarvāṇi bhūtāni paritrāsam upāgaman
english: Seeing it blazing like the fire of Time arrived at the end of an age, all beings were overcome with terror.

sanskrit: sadevāsuragandharvaṃ samuniṃ sāpsarogaṇam jagad dhi sarvam asvasthaṃ pitāmaham upasthitam
english: The entire world — with gods, Asuras, Gandharvas, sages, and hosts of Apsarases — was uneasy and approached the Grandsire.

sanskrit: ūcuś ca devadeveśaṃ varadaṃ prapitāmaham kaccil lokakṣayo deva prāpto vā yugasaṃkayaḥ
english: And they said to the god of gods, the boon-granting great-grandsire: "Has the dissolution of the worlds come, O god, or the conflagration of the age?"

sanskrit: nedṛśaṃ dṛṣṭapūrvaṃ na śrutaṃ vā prapitāmaha devānāṃ bhayasaṃmoho lokānāṃ saṃkṣayaḥ prabho
english: "Such a thing has never been seen or heard before, O great-grandsire — the terror and bewilderment of the gods, the destruction of the worlds, O lord."

sanskrit: teṣāṃ tad vacanaṃ śrutvā brahmā lokapitāmanaḥ bhayakāraṇam ācaṣṭe devānām abhayaṃkaraḥ
english: Hearing those words, Brahmā, the grandsire of the worlds, who dispels fear, declared to the gods the cause of their terror.

sanskrit: vadhāya lavaṇasyājau śaraḥ śatrughnadhāritaḥ tejasā yasya sarve sma saṃmūḍhāḥ surasattamāḥ
english: "For the slaying of Lavaṇa in battle, the arrow held by Śatrughna — by whose radiance all you best of gods have been bewildered —"

sanskrit: eṣo hi pūrvaṃ devasya lokakartuḥ sanātanaḥ śaras tejomayo vatsā yena vai bhayam āgatam
english: "— this is the primordial, eternal, radiant arrow of the god who created the worlds, dear ones, by which this fear has come upon you."

sanskrit: eṣa vai kaiṭabhasyārthe madhunaś ca mahāśaraḥ sṛṣṭo mahātmanā tena vadhārthaṃ daityayos tayoḥ
english: "This great arrow was created by that great-souled one for the sake of slaying Kaiṭabha and Madhu — for the destruction of those two Daityas."

sanskrit: evam etaṃ prajānīdhvaṃ viṣṇos tejomayaṃ śaram eṣā caiva tanuḥ pūrvā viṣṇos tasya mahātmanaḥ
english: "Know this to be the radiant arrow of Viṣṇu; and this Śatrughna is likewise the former body of that great-souled Viṣṇu."

sanskrit: ito gacchatā paśyadhvaṃ vadhyamānaṃ mahātmanā rāmānujena vīreṇa lavaṇaṃ rākṣasottamam
english: "Go from here and witness the foremost of rākṣasas, Lavaṇa, being slain by the great-souled hero, the younger brother of Rāma."

sanskrit: tasya te devadevasya niśamya madhurāṃ giram ājagmur yatra yudhyete śatrughnalavaṇāv ubhau
english: Hearing those sweet words of the god of gods, they went to the place where Śatrughna and Lavaṇa were both fighting.

sanskrit: taṃ śaraṃ divyasaṃkāśaṃ śatrughnakaradhāritam dadṛśuḥ sarvabhūtāni yugāntāgnim ivotthitam
english: All beings saw that arrow, divine in appearance, held in Śatrughna's hand, risen like the conflagration at the end of an age.

sanskrit: ākāśam āvṛtaṃ dṛṣṭvā devair hi raghunandanaḥ siṃhanādaṃ muhuḥ kṛtvā dadarśa lavaṇaṃ punaḥ
english: Seeing the sky filled with gods, the son of Raghu's line roared repeatedly with the roar of a lion and beheld Lavaṇa once more.

sanskrit: āhūtaś ca tatas tena śatrughnena mahātmanā lavaṇaḥ krodhasaṃyukto yuddhāya samupasthitaḥ
english: Challenged by the great-souled Śatrughna, Lavaṇa, filled with rage, presented himself for battle.

sanskrit: ākarṇāt sa vikṛṣyātha tad dhanur dhanvināṃ varaḥ sa mumoca mahābāṇaṃ lavaṇasya mahorasi uras tasya vidāryāśu praviveśa rasātalam
english: Drawing that bow to his ear, that best of archers released the great arrow at Lavaṇa's broad chest; cleaving his chest swiftly, it entered the netherworld.

sanskrit: gatvā rasātalaṃ divyaṃ śaro vibudhapūjitaḥ punar evāgamat tūrṇam ikṣvākukulanandanam
english: Having gone to the divine netherworld, that arrow, worshipped by the gods, swiftly returned again to the delight of the Ikṣvāku lineage.

sanskrit: śatrughnaśaranirbhinno lavaṇaḥ sa niśācaraḥ papāta sahasā bhūmau vajrāhata ivācalaḥ
english: Pierced through by Śatrughna's arrow, that night-roaming Lavaṇa fell suddenly to the ground like a mountain struck by the thunderbolt.

sanskrit: tac ca divyaṃ mahac chūlaṃ hate lavaṇarākṣase paśyatāṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ rudrasya vaśam anvagāt
english: And that great divine trident, when the rākṣasa Lavaṇa was slain, in the sight of all beings, returned to the power of Rudra.

sanskrit: ekeṣupātena bhayaṃ nihatya lokatrayasyāsya raghupravīraḥ vinirbabhāv udyatacāpabāṇas tamaḥ praṇudyeva sahasraraśmiḥ
english: Having slain with a single arrow the terror of all three worlds, the foremost hero of Raghu's line shone forth with bow and arrow raised, even as the thousand-rayed sun dispels darkness.

sanskrit: hate tu lavaṇe devāḥ sendrāḥ sāgnipurogamāḥ ūcuḥ sumadhurāṃ vāṇīṃ śatrughnāṃ śatrutāpanam
english: When Lavaṇa was slain, the gods — with Indra at their head and Agni foremost among them — spoke sweet words to Śatrughna, scorcher of enemies.

sanskrit: diṣṭyā te vijayo vatsa diṣṭya lavaṇarākṣasaḥ hataḥ puruṣaśārdūlavaraṃ varaya rāghava
english: "By good fortune is your victory, dear one; by good fortune the rākṣasa Lavaṇa is slain. O best among tigers of men, O Rāghava, ask a boon."

sanskrit: varadāḥ sma mahābāho sarva eva samāgatāḥ vijayākāṅkṣiṇas tubhyam amoghaṃ darśanaṃ hi naḥ
english: "We are all gathered here as granters of boons, O mighty-armed one, desiring your victory; indeed our vision is never without fruit."

sanskrit: devānāṃ bhāṣitaṃ śrutvā śūro mūrdhni kṛtāñjaliḥ pratyuvāca mahābāhuḥ śatrughnaḥ prayatātmavān
english: Hearing the words of the gods, the valiant, great-armed Śatrughna, with hands joined above his head, replied with a disciplined mind.

sanskrit: imāṃ madhupurīṃ ramyāṃ madhurāṃ deva nirmitām niveśaṃ prapnuyāṃ śīghram eṣa me 'stu varo mataḥ
english: "Let me quickly establish settlement in this lovely Madhupurī, sweet Madhurā, created by the gods — this let my boon be, so I think."

sanskrit: taṃ devāḥ prītamanaso bāḍham ity eva rāghavam bhaviṣyati purī ramyā śūrasenā na saṃśayaḥ
english: The gods, with hearts full of joy, said "So be it" to the Rāghava: "A lovely city it shall be — Śūrasenā, without doubt."

sanskrit: te tathoktvā mahātmāno divam āruruhus tadā śatrughno 'pi mahātejās tāṃ senāṃ samupānayat
english: Having spoken thus, those great-souled ones ascended to heaven; and the greatly radiant Śatrughna brought up his army.

sanskrit: sā sena śīghram āgacchac chrutvā śatrughnaśāsanam niveśanaṃ ca śatrughnaḥ śāsanena samārabhat
english: That army came quickly on hearing Śatrughna's command, and Śatrughna began the founding of the settlement by his decree.

sanskrit: sā purī divyasaṃkāśā varṣe dvādaśame śubhā niviṣṭā śūrasenānāṃ viṣayaś cākutobhayaḥ
english: That city, divine in appearance, auspicious, was established in the twelfth year, and the territory of the Śūrasenas became free from all fear.

sanskrit: kṣetrāṇi sasya yuktāni kāle varṣati vāsavaḥ arogā vīrapuruṣā śatrughnabhujapālitā
english: The fields were full of crops, Indra rained in season, the people were free of disease and vigorous, protected by the arms of Śatrughna.

sanskrit: ardhacandrapratīkāśā yamunātīraśobhitā śobhitā gṛhamukhyaiś ca śobhitā catvarāpaṇaiḥ
english: Shaped like a half-moon, graced by the bank of the Yamunā, adorned with foremost mansions, adorned with market squares and bazaars.

sanskrit: yac ca tena mahac chūnyaṃ lavaṇena kṛtaṃ purā śobhayām āsa tad vīro nānāpaṇyasamṛddhibhiḥ
english: Whatever great emptiness had been made by Lavaṇa formerly, the hero beautified that with abundance of various commodities.

sanskrit: tāṃ samṛddhāṃ samṛddhārthaḥ śatrughno bharatānujaḥ nirīkṣya paramaprītaḥ paraṃ harṣam upāgamat
english: Śatrughna, the younger brother of Bharata, himself prosperous in wealth, surveyed that prosperous city and was supremely pleased, overcome with supreme joy.

sanskrit: tasya buddhiḥ samutpannā niveśya madhurāṃ purīm rāmapādau nirīkṣeyaṃ varṣe dvādaśame śubhe
english: The thought arose in his mind: having established the city of Madhurā, "I should behold the feet of Rāma in this auspicious twelfth year."

sanskrit: tato dvādaśame varṣe śatrughno rāmapālitām ayodhyāṃ cakame gantum alpabhṛtyabalānugaḥ
english: Then, in the twelfth year, Śatrughna desired to go to Ayodhyā, protected by Rāma, accompanied by a small retinue and force.

sanskrit: mantriṇo balamukhyāṃś ca nivartya ca purodhasaṃ jagāma rathamukhyena hayayuktena bhāsvatā
english: Having dismissed his ministers, the chiefs of the army, and the chaplain, he went in a splendid chariot harnessed with horses.

sanskrit: sa gatvā gaṇitān vāsān saptāṣṭau raghunandanaḥ ayodhyām agamat tūrṇaṃ rāghavotsukadarśanaḥ
english: Traversing seven or eight calculated stages of travel, the son of Raghu's line quickly reached Ayodhyā, eager to behold the Rāghava.

sanskrit: sa praviśya purīṃ ramyāṃ śrīmān ikṣvākunandanaḥ praviveśa mahābāhur yatra rāmo mahādyutiḥ
english: Entering the lovely city, that glorious, great-armed delight of the Ikṣvāku line went to where the greatly resplendent Rāma was.

sanskrit: so 'bhivādya mahātmānaṃ jvalantam iva tejasā uvāca prāñjalir bhūtvā rāmaṃ satyaparākramam
english: He saluted the great-souled one blazing as it were with energy, and standing with palms joined, spoke to Rāma of true valour.

sanskrit: yad ājñaptaṃ mahārāja sarvaṃ tat kṛtavān aham hataḥ sa lavaṇaḥ pāpaḥ purī sā ca niveśitā
english: "Whatever was commanded, O great king, all of that I have done: that wicked Lavaṇa is slain, and that city has been established."

sanskrit: dvādaśaṃ ca gataṃ varṣaṃ tvāṃ vinā raghunandana notsaheyam ahaṃ vastuṃ tvayā virahito nṛpa
english: "Twelve years have passed without you, O delight of Raghu's line; I could not bear to dwell separated from you, O king."

sanskrit: sa me prasādaṃ kākutstha kuruṣvāmitavikrama mātṛhīno yathā vatsas tvāṃ vinā pravasāmy aham
english: "Grant me your favour, O Kākutstha, O you of boundless valour; without you I wander abroad like a calf bereft of its mother."

sanskrit: evaṃ bruvāṇaṃ śatrughnaṃ pariṣvajyedam abravīt mā viṣādaṃ kṛthā vīra naitat kṣatriya ceṣṭitam
english: Embracing Śatrughna who spoke thus, Rāma said: "Do not grieve, O hero; this is not the conduct befitting a kṣatriya."

sanskrit: nāvasīdanti rājāno vipravāseṣu rāghava prajāś ca paripālyā hi kṣatradharmeṇa rāghava
english: "Kings do not despair during sojourns abroad, O Rāghava; and subjects must be protected through the dharma of the kṣatriya, O Rāghava."

sanskrit: kāle kāle ca māṃ vīra ayodhyām avalokitum āgaccha tvaṃ naraśreṣṭha gantāsi ca puraṃ tava
english: "Come to Ayodhyā to see me from time to time, O hero, O best of men, and then return to your own city."

sanskrit: mamāpi tvaṃ sudayitaḥ prāṇair api na saṃśayaḥ avaśyaṃ karaṇīyaṃ ca rājyasya paripālanam
english: "You are dearer to me even than life itself, without doubt; yet the protection of the kingdom must inevitably be carried out."

sanskrit: tasmāt tvaṃ vasa kākutstha pañcarātraṃ mayā saha ūrdhvaṃ gantāsi madhurāṃ sabhṛtyabalavāhanaḥ
english: "Therefore, O Kākutstha, dwell with me for five nights; after that you shall go to Madhurā with your servants, army, and conveyances."

sanskrit: rāmasyaitad vacaḥ śrutvā dharmayuktaṃ mano'nugam śatrughno dīnayā vācā bāḍham ity eva cābravīt
english: Hearing these words of Rāma, righteous and pleasing to the mind, Śatrughna said with a sorrowful voice, "So be it."

sanskrit: sa pañcarātraṃ kākutstho rāghavasya yathājñayā uṣya tatra maheṣvāso gamanāyopacakrame
english: That mighty archer, the Kākutstha, having dwelt there five nights by the Rāghava's command, made ready for departure.

sanskrit: āmantrya tu mahātmānaṃ rāmaṃ satyaparākramam bharataṃ lakṣmaṇaṃ caiva mahāratham upāruhat
english: Having taken leave of the great-souled Rāma of true valour, and of Bharata and Lakṣmaṇa as well, he mounted his great chariot.

sanskrit: dūraṃ tābhyām anugato lakṣmaṇena mahātmanā bharatena ca śatrughno jagāmāśu purīṃ tadā
english: Accompanied for a long distance by the great-souled Lakṣmaṇa and by Bharata, Śatrughna then quickly went to his city.
